original.target_description: Study 8: surname versus full-name reference, share of NSF career-award money, fixed effect in mixed-effects model.

n.exclusions: Incomplete study and attention-check failures excluded per primary replication report Sample section; original per-study count printed.
n.quote: In study 8 ( n = 554), we tested whether researchers referred to by surname (vs. full name) are judged as more deserving of a fictitious NSF career award and award-related funds.

es.quote: Researchers referred to by surname were also allocated a larger share of the award money by 6%: F (1,551) = 4.61, P = 0.032

p.quote: Researchers referred to by surname were also allocated a larger share of the award money by 6%: F (1,551) = 4.61, P = 0.032

replication.target_description: Hypothesis to replicate and bet on: Researchers referred to by surname are allocated a larger share of the award money compared to researchers who are referred to by their full name. To evaluate this hypothesis, the authors use a test of fixed effects in a mixed-effects model controlling for the specific proposal and researcher name: F(1,551) = 4.61, p = 0.032 (Fig. 3); p. 7281.

n.sample_role: participants in focal analysis after exclusions
n.exclusions: Since the experiment was expected to take, on average, 5 minutes, we had a show-up fee of $1. Overall, we sampled 3427 eligible participants (i.e., participants who passed the IP quality checks, provided informed consent, and passed the common attention check). However, as indicated in the report, we excluded all individuals from the analysis who did not pass the attention check from the original experiment (indicating that the study is about science). 578 out of 3427 individuals did not correctly answer this attention check, which led to our final analysis sample of 2849 participants. While we followed the pre-registered analysis exactly, the replication result is based on a z-test due to differences in the optimization routines implemented in different software applications (the replication result has been estimated in Stata, the original result in SPSS).

reported_success.quote: Given the criteria and procedure outlined above, the hypothesis of interest has not been replicated at a significance level of p < 0.05.
